ledger.note: 1983: the SPLA rises in the south. The SPLA was founded in 1983 'to reestablish an autonomous southern Sudan by fighting against the central government'; 'In May 1983, the 1st Division's 105th Battalion in the Sudanese military mutinied in the towns of Bor and Pibor' (infobox start of the war 5 June 1983). The page does not say what land the SPLA held at the start, so only the Bor-Pibor area is drawn; the first run drew the whole south from the undated 'large areas' sentence.
1983: the war for the south begins (infobox 5 June 1983).

notes: A rebel state Cliopatria lacks, the southern counterpart of republic-of-sudan's 1983-2005 contest events. Fix run of 2026-10-24: the 1983 land is cut to the Bor-Pibor area and the 'large areas' sentence, undated and set after the 1989 coup, becomes a 1989 gain (confidence 1; the reviewer read it as confidence 2, the page does not date it); the July 1992 loss of Torit and Eastern Equatoria and the 1997 gain are keyframe steps; the dissolve of January 2005 goes to republic-of-sudan, not south-sudan (a state from 2011), because Sudan keeps the south 2005-2011. The capital is Torit, the only headquarters the page names (lost July 1992). The pages give no leader list and no dated extent of SPLA control other than 1992 and 1997, so rulers are empty. The rebels' later governance of the south (2005-2011) is not described on the pages opened; the First Sudanese Civil War rebels (1955-1972) are not covered (the page names no land they held). Gazetteer: Torit is not in the places table.
